requirement:
In authored chapters, requirements, examples, and named definitions render as
collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens. Body prose shares the
containing prose's left edge without added indentation. Each header's badge
is right-aligned and identifies the declaration and its kind.
A narrow colored bar in the right margin delineates the section and uses the
badge's color: blue for requirements, purple for examples, and green for named
definitions. Named definitions use the same badge styling, displaying their
kind and phrase. A square disclosure control at the top of that bar adjoins
the badge without a gap, matches its height, and is separated from it by a thin
border. The same thin divider separates the badge's kind from its name or
phrase. The badge and control form a rectangle with subtly rounded outer
corners and straight internal joins; the vertical bar has rounded ends.
The control shows a minus when expanded and a plus when collapsed. Collapsing
a section hides its body while keeping the header visible. The disclosure
works with a mouse or keyboard.

The body retains its Markdown rendering, including code blocks and nested
declarations. Requirement and example headers retain the definition and
evidence links described by {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; those
links navigate independently of the disclosure.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.index.declaration_sections` that needs implementation evidence. Every clause describes rendered, observable behavior, and each could be met by a different construction.

- **Collapsible and expanded on open:** "render as collapsible sections, expanded when the chapter opens". A `<details open>/<summary>` element would work. So would a div with a script toggle, with the same result for readers. The element choice is discretionary.
- **Body alignment:** "Body prose shares the containing prose's left edge without added indentation". This is visual layout.
- **Badge, bar, colors, control and borders:** the clauses on the right-aligned badge, the blue, purple and green bar, the square control that adjoins the badge and matches its height, the thin dividers, and the rounded corners and bar ends. These specify appearance only. A `::before` bar, a border or a background gradient would give the same pixels. The CSS selectors are not prescribed.
- **Minus and plus indicator and keyboard use:** these are observable. The text does not require a particular mechanism, such as a pseudo-element or an icon font.
- **Body keeps its Markdown rendering, and header links work independently of the disclosure:** the requirement cites `requirements.index.navigation` for these links, and that requirement owns their structure. Here the text asks only that the links navigate independently of the disclosure.

The supplied root `md/habeas.css` has rules for `.habeas-declaration`, its `summary` and `::after`, and the badge classes. They are one way to produce this appearance. No clause prescribes a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface that they would have to match. Whether the rendering is correct is a question for the behavioral or visual checks, not for structural implementation coverage.

behavioral: I judged the tests against the subject text only. I did not read implementation source, and I did not run the tests. The rendering and stylesheet assertions below cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.index.declaration_sections`.

**Sections and open state**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_sections_contain_their_headers_and_markdown_bodies]` renders a requirement, a nested example and a definition through `preprocess_book`.
- It asserts exactly three `<details class="habeas-declaration"` elements, each with the `open` attribute, and matching `<summary>` and `</details>` counts.
- It asserts that surrounding prose (`Before.` / `After.`) sits outside the sections.

**Header and body**
- The same test checks that both header links are inside `</summary>` and the body is not.
- Header checks: the kind link has its anchor and aria-label, and the name link goes to the evidence page. No `habeas-detail-icon` is present. These are the `requirements.index.navigation` links the section text says headers keep.
- Body checks: the body sits in `habeas-declaration-body` and keeps rendered Markdown (`<strong>`, `<em>`, a `language-rust` code block). A nested `<details>` is rendered and closes correctly.
- Hiding the body while the header stays visible follows from this split. The header is in `summary` and the body is outside it.
- The links navigate independently of the disclosure because they are anchors inside the summary. No test could add evidence for this beyond the markup checks.

**Badge and colors**
- `fn[declaration_badges_and_margin_controls_share_kind_colors]` asserts the `--habeas-declaration-color` style per kind: `006ba8` for req, `7151a1` for example and `2e8555` for definition. It also checks the `habeas-badge-name` class.
- The sections test asserts that the definition badge shows its kind and its phrase (`alpha & beta`) in the same badge structure.

**Layout and styling**
- `fn[declaration_badge_stylesheet_keeps_split_links_in_one_row]` asserts `justify-content: flex-end`, which right-aligns the badge. It also asserts the non-wrapping row.
- `fn[declaration_styles_distinguish_disclosure_state_and_keyboard_focus]` covers the rest of the CSS:
  - Margin bar: a 3px `::before` bar with `border-radius: 2px` and the declaration color, positioned in the right margin.
  - Body indentation: no body padding, and the section margin and padding are asserted.
  - Disclosure control: square (width equals height, equal to `--habeas-badge-height`), `gap: 0`, a thin `var(--bg)` left border, and radius `0 3px 3px 0`. It is layered over the bar.
  - Badge shape: the kind segment has radius `3px 0 0 3px`. The name segment has radius 0 and a 1px divider. This gives rounded outer corners and straight internal joins.
  - Control state: `+` when collapsed, `−` under `[open]`.
  - Keyboard: a `:focus-visible` outline on the control. The native `<summary>` also makes it work with a keyboard.
- `fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]` covers `replace_definitions`, the lower-level rendering step. It checks that a body with a heading and a code block keeps its Markdown.

The tests assert real outcomes rather than just running the code. I found no obligation without a test and no marking gap, since all relevant tests carry `{test}` for the subject.

:::{req} navigation
Each requirement and example declaration badge has two adjacent links. Its
kind (`req` or `example`) links to the declaration's anchor on the current
page; its full name links to the evidence detail page. These segments stay
together in one non-wrapping row, with no separate arrow link or plaintext evidence link.
Each detail page links back to the declaration's anchored badge and to the
index. Reference badges continue to link to the declaration. These links
resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in
`requirements.cli.mdbook`.
